Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO, Elysian), Devon Kim (Lead Engineer, Elysian), Samir Patel (Security, Elysian)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Elysian Health through SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth options, environment setup, and Console/Optimize recommendations. Elysian expressed concern about PHI handling, VPC/private deployment, and latency/cost tradeoffs for inference on clinical note summarization. Agreed next steps: share quickstart repo, security docs, pricing, and schedule pilot benchmark.
topics: Auth and env vars (API key, SSO)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey all, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, joining with Priya our SE. Uh, how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Doing well, Jordan, thanks. We'll kick off from our side, quick intros - I'm Marta, CTO. Devon is our lead on integrations, and Samir focuses on security and compliance.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great. Today we'll run through the SDK quickstarts in Python and TypeScript, show how auth and env setup works, and surface a few Optimize levers for cost/latency.
[00:27] Priya Patel: Hi all - I'll screen share shortly, show a small code example, pip/npm quickstart, then demo a short end-to-end request and streaming response.
[00:35] Devon Kim: Sounds good. Our main use case is clinical note summarization - PHI sensitive. We'll need to understand data residency and private deployment options.
[00:42] Samir Patel: And encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC 2 is a must.
[00:47] Priya Patel: Understood. We support hosted API for quick testing, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private/VPC options for regulated workloads. We have SOC 2 reports and KMS integrations - I'll link the docs after.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: Quick agenda: 1) show Python quickstart, 2) TS quickstart, 3) auth patterns (API key, SSO), 4) Console & Optimize highlights, 5) Q&A and next steps.
[01:10] Priya Patel: Ok I'm sharing. First, pip install redwood-inference - typical flow is set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, then instantiate a client: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), region='us-west-2') and call client.chat.create(...) or client.generate(...).
[01:32] Devon Kim: So REDWOOD_API_KEY is long-lived? We prefer short-lived tokens or something SSO-friendly.
[01:38] Priya Patel: Good Q. Hosted API supports API keys and token rotation; for enterprise Private deployments we integrate with SAML/SSO and can issue short-lived tokens via your identity provider. We also support ephemeral creds for CI.
[01:51] Samir Patel: And for on-prem we manage the control plane separately and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[01:56] Priya Patel: Correct - Private installs can use customer KMS; we document HSM options. I'll add the KMS/HSM section in the security doc.
[02:05] Priya Patel: Back to code: example Python snippet - paste: from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-compat-small', prompt='Summarize these notes for a clinician', max_tokens=150)
print(resp.text)
[02:30] Devon Kim: Ok, does the SDK automatically stream tokens? We need progressive display when users read a summary.
[02:36] Priya Patel: Yep - both SDKs support streaming. In Python you can iterate over resp.stream() and in TS you can use client.chat.stream() to pipe tokens to the UI. Streaming works with our hosted and Dedicated runtimes.
[02:47] Jordan Lee: Priya will also show the TS example.
[02:51] Priya Patel: Switching to TypeScript: npm install @redwood/inference
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-small', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the following clinical note...' }] })
console.log(res.output)
[03:20] Marta Ruiz: Are there recommended models for clinical summarization - tuned ones or do we self-evaluate?
[03:27] Priya Patel: We have a model catalog with profile metadata - latency and quality baselines. For PHI, many customers prefer quantized open models on Dedicated or Private to avoid vendor model exposures. We can recommend variants and share eval results.
[03:40] Devon Kim: Performance-wise, we expect peaks of ~200 qps during batch ingestion windows and lower during interactive use. What are the batching suggestions?
[03:49] Priya Patel: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching sizes and KV/prefix caching for your workload. For summarization, batching multiple notes into one request or using streaming with smaller batch windows helps. We'll run a workload analysis during the pilot.
[03:59] Samir Patel: On compliance, we need audit logs for who requested what and token-level telemetry.
[04:05] Priya Patel: Console provides per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs. For Private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[04:13] Jordan Lee: Quick note on network topology: VPC peering or private connectivity is available for Dedicated/Private. For HIPAA/PHI customers we recommend Private or Dedicated in a customer-controlled VPC.
[04:25] Devon Kim: Cool - what about latency targets? We need sub-300ms 95th for short prompts, ideally.
[04:31] Priya Patel: Achieving sub-300ms 95th is possible with optimized kernels, shorter context windows, and hardware choices - we can propose Dedicated with pinned GPUs and pre-warmed KV cache. There is always a trade-off with cost.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: I'll walk through the Console quick look. Priya, can you hop to the dashboard?
[04:50] Priya Patel: Sure. (screen share) Here's the model route page, you can see per-route SLOs, cost per token, and latency histograms. The rollout features allow canary to a new model and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes.
[05:06] Devon Kim: Nice - can we set automatic fallback if a model exceeds error rate?
[05:10] Priya Patel: Yes, rules based on latency, error thresholds, or capacity. You can also route by geo or tier.
[05:16] Marta Ruiz: Back to dev flow - how do we do local dev without hitting prod keys?
[05:21] Priya Patel: Use the sandbox project with limited quota and test API keys. We provide a CLI to create ephemeral tokens for local sessions and CI. Also can run a local SDK mock for unit tests.
[05:32] Jordan Lee: Example env setup for Python: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx; export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2; then run python quickstart.py. For TS similarly set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[05:45] Devon Kim: Are there rate limits on hosted tiers? We might need bursts during nightly jobs.
[05:50] Priya Patel: Hosted has quota and throttles; Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies with reserved throughput. We'll outline commit tiers in the pricing doc.
[05:59] Samir Patel: Any encryption specifics for data in transit and at rest?
[06:03] Priya Patel: TLS in transit, and data at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS for Private installs; for hosted we provide encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS is available for enterprise plans.
[06:15] Jordan Lee: Let's demo a short end-to-end: Python quickstart hitting hosted endpoint with streaming. Priya will run a sample summarization request.
[06:22] Priya Patel: Running now... (typing) 
[06:30] Priya Patel: Output shows progressive tokens; you can see token delta coming in. Example response: "Summarized: Patient presented with...". There may be minor transcription artifacts when we demo on this call.
[06:44] Devon Kim: Looks good. If we want to reduce cost per token, can we quantize?
[06:49] Priya Patel: Absolutely - Optimize can recommend quantized model variants that reduce GPU memory and token cost while measuring quality impact. We often recommend 4-bit quantization for batch workloads.
[06:59] Marta Ruiz: For PHI, are models trained on customer data? We want to ensure no model retraining with our data unless we opt in.
[07:06] Priya Patel: We do not train public models on customer data by default. For special arrangements we have fine-tuning/private tuning options under contract, with clear data residency and consent.
[07:17] Samir Patel: Good. On logging, can we get token-level redaction before logs leave our environment?
[07:23] Priya Patel: For Private deployments you can configure redaction pipelines and push logs only to your SIEM. For hosted we provide redaction options and allow customers to opt-out of retaining request payloads.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: Devon, operationally what's your timeline for a pilot?
[07:40] Devon Kim: We want a pilot within two weeks, run a benchmark with our ingestion pipeline, and validate latency / cost. If that looks good, push to a canary in prod.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: Great - we'll set up a 1-hr benchmarking session. I'll send available slots.
[07:52] Priya Patel: One thing to call out: SDKs also support structured output and function-calling patterns if you need JSON schemas for downstream processing.
[07:59] Devon Kim: We'll probably use structured outputs for downstream EHR ingestion.
[08:04] Marta Ruiz: Any gotchas integrating with Node servers in our infra (we run serverless lambdas)?
[08:09] Priya Patel: For serverless, use streaming and small batch sizes to avoid cold start costs, and consider ephemeral clients per invocation. We have examples in the quickstart for AWS Lambda.
[08:20] Samir Patel: About network - do you support private endpoints for zero public egress?
[08:24] Priya Patel: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can configure private endpoints and VPC peering, so no public egress is required.
[08:33] Jordan Lee: I'll mention pricing briefly - hosted pay-as-you-go per-token, Dedicated reserved monthly with commit tiers, and Private pricing is license plus support. I'll send a detailed sheet.
[08:45] Devon Kim: Can you include an estimate for our projected 200 qps peak?
[08:49] Jordan Lee: Yes we'll include capacity estimates and cost scenarios in the pricing attachment.
[08:55] Marta Ruiz: On SOC 2, can we get the report and do you support periodic audits?
[08:59] Priya Patel: We can share SOC 2 Type II report and compliance pack. For Private we can assist with audit evidence shipping.
[09:08] Samir Patel: One more - SLA and uptime for Dedicated?
[09:12] Jordan Lee: Dedicated has SLA options with uptime and latency targets; exact terms are in the enterprise addendum.
[09:18] Priya Patel: Wrapping up, the quickstarts repo link I'll share contains examples: python/quickstart.py, ts/quickstart.mjs, a local mock server, and CI token rotation example.
[09:31] Devon Kim: Perfect. We'll try the quickstart and push some sample payloads.
[09:35] Jordan Lee: Any other questions?
[09:38] Marta Ruiz: Not right now. Thanks - we'll review and follow up.
[09:41] Jordan Lee: Great - recap of next steps: Priya share quickstart and security docs; Jordan send pricing + capacity scenarios; schedule pilot benchmark; Samir to send security Qs; Devon to share sample payloads.
[09:56] Priya Patel: I'll drop the links in the follow-up email and include the sandbox creds for testing.
[10:02] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[10:06] Marta Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[10:08] (call ends)
